$comment: Parcel Yatra iPhone PWA — presentation and install metadata for the web export.
This is not an Expo app config. The Expo project, its screens and its routes stay in
apps/mobile/app.json and are exported for web by scripts/build.mjs; nothing here is read by
Expo. What lives here is the part a browser needs that React Native has no word for: the
manifest, the icons, the iOS status-bar and viewport metadata, and the install guidance copy.
Edit this file, re-run `npm run build -w @py/ios-pwa`, and dist/ reflects it.
name: Parcel Yatra
description: Send a parcel across the country on a traveller's already-planned journey.

serviceWorker.$comment: Only the hashed bundles, the images and the shell are precached. See service-worker.js for the rules and ios/PARITY.md for why API traffic is excluded.

installGuide.title: Add Parcel Yatra to your Home Screen
installGuide.body: Install it like an app: full screen, its own icon, no Safari bar.
steps: Tap the Share icon in Safari's bottom bar.
Scroll up and choose Add to Home Screen.

updateBanner.title: A new version of Parcel Yatra is ready

$comment: EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL decides which backend the exported bundle talks to, and it is read
at build time, so it is baked into dist/. Set it in the hosting environment, not here; this
value is only the fallback for a plain local build.
A value starting with '/' is same-origin: recommended, because the HttpOnly session cookie is
then first-party and survives iOS Safari's tracking prevention. See README.md section 5.
